title: Quantization regression gatekeeper & calibration playbook
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Deliver a reproducible, workload-aware playbook and automated gatekeeper for detecting quality regressions introduced by quantization profile changes (int8/int4) and AWQ/GPTQ conversion steps. The goal is to enforce per-workload quality SLOs before allowing a quantized model into production, and to provide calibrated, statistically-sound thresholds and automated rollback triggers.
background: Recent Dedicated customer incidents surfaced subtle regressions after an int4 AWQ conversion for a high-QPS reranking route. Existing eval runs measure average perplexity and a handful of synthetic tasks but lack workload-specific baselines, noise-aware thresholds, and an automated gate that ties into rollout policies. This ticket consolidates learnings and builds the detection + calibration tooling.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable eval harness that runs AWQ and GPTQ conversions and compares outputs to full-precision baselines across defined workload suites
Automated statistical tests (bootstrap/paired t-test) with configurable alpha to determine significant regressions
Per-route delta budgets and noise-aware thresholds stored in the model metadata and surfaced to Console
A gatekeeper service that emits pass/fail per build and blocks auto-rollout when regressions exceed budgets
Integration tests and a canary rollback policy exercised in staging with a mock customer workload

decisions: Use paired bootstrap confidence intervals as the primary statistical signal (resilient to non-normal metric distributions)
Maintain separate delta budgets per metric class: task accuracy (EM/F1/Rouge), perplexity, and generation quality heuristics (toxicity/fluency scores)
Represent thresholds as 3-tuple: nominal_delta, safety_buffer, min_samples_required — stored as model metadata key quant:regression_threshold
Gatekeeper will be a lightweight service invoked by CI and the rollout controller; failing gates mark build as 'block' and create a follow-up ticket automatically
AWQ conversions get a stricter safety_buffer than GPTQ for now based on observed variance in initial experiments
eval_plan: 1) Define workload suites: reranking (customer A), chat (internal synthetic prompts), summarization (CNN/DM subset). 2) For each model + conversion (FP16->AWQ int4, FP16->GPTQ int8), run paired queries and collect metric vectors. 3) Compute paired bootstrap CI for delta metric; flag if lower bound exceeds nominal_delta + safety_buffer. 4) Run robustness probes (noisy inputs, long contexts) to detect distributional fragility. 5) Save fingerprints (input token length distribution, top-k token frequency) alongside results.
metrics_and_alerts: Primary metrics: Exact Match (EM), F1, ROUGE-L, generation perplexity, average token logprob, and a customer-defined rubric for ranking routes. Derivative signals: per-request latency change (+/-), cost-per-token delta. Alerts: Datadog alert when >5% of recent builds fail gate OR when a single route exceeds its delta budget in production for 3 consecutive deploys.
rollout_policy: If gate fails in CI: block automatic canary rollout and create 'quant-regression-block' ticket assigned to model owner. Manual override allowed only after a documented risk acceptance and a second independent eval. For staged canaries: if regression observed in 5% production traffic beyond threshold, automatic rollback to previous model version and incident ping to SRE.
test_plan: Unit tests for bootstrap CI code, integration test that runs a small synthetic workload through gatekeeper in CI (mocking AWQ/GPTQ conversions), E2E staging run demonstrates automated rollback on failing gate. Performance test ensures gatekeeper adds <30s overhead to CI pipelines for standard model sizes.
next_steps: 1) Complete validation of bootstrap implementation and land PR #4321. 2) Finalize threshold defaults with Research and PM by 2025-03-10. 3) Wire gatekeeper to rollout controller and create UX ticket for Console visualization of per-model thresholds. 4) Schedule staging canary for 2025-03-17.
notes: Avoid setting overly-tight thresholds that will cause operational churn. Thresholds are expected to be tuned per-customer over time; the first rollout will be conservative. Keep a human-in-the-loop for first three production incidents after enabling automatic rollback.
